sample_unit: community-dwelling participants aged 65-85 with in-home ECG and echocardiography

links.outcome: AI-ECG discrimination in community population versus hospital-based derivation cohort
links.effect: AUC 71% (95% CI 66%-76%) in PREVUE-VALVE vs 83% (95% CI 82%-83%) in hospital cohort; SHD prevalence 8% vs 43%; propensity matching attenuated but did not eliminate the difference.
links.quote: Consistent with these differences, model discrimination was lower in PREVUE-VALVE than in the hospital-based cohort (AUC: 71% [95% CI: 66%-76%] vs 83% [95% CI: 82%-83%]).

links.outcome: AI-ECG performance in a new population compared to developer-reported hospital performance
links.effect: AUC fell to 71% in community cohort from 83% in hospital cohort; performance similar across external hospital cohorts, indicating disease spectrum drives the drop.
links.quote: Consistent with these differences, model discrimination was lower in PREVUE-VALVE than in the hospital-based cohort (AUC: 71% [95% CI: 66%-76%] vs 83% [95% CI: 82%-83%]).

links.outcome: Model performance when extended to a new population with lower prevalence and milder disease
links.effect: AUC 71% in community-dwelling adults vs 83% in hospital cohort; higher in subgroups with abnormal ECG (79%) or impaired health status (76%).
links.quote: In a community-dwelling population with lower disease prevalence and milder phenotypes, AI-ECG performance was attenuated relative to hospital-based cohorts, driven by differences in disease spectrum.

screen.reason: The study directly evaluates the transportability and spectrum effects of deploying a hospital-trained AI diagnostic tool into a community setting, demonstrating the necessity of local setting/population validation before deployment.

primary.practice: local validation in intended deployment setting
